papers.title_en: Curriculum-Based Adversarial Heterogeneous Agent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Quad-Copter Landing in Maritime Settings
papers.authors: Allan Minh-Tam Nguyen, Sree Showrya Kotala, Stefan Banioi-Crijman, Kurt Driessens, Rico Möckel
papers.evidence: 用HAPPO多智能体强化学习实现四旋翼空中捕获
papers.tldr: 海上回收无人机面临风湍流与船甲板运动干扰，传统着陆方法常不可靠。本文在NVIDIA Isaac Lab中，采用课程学习与对抗风智能体，基于异构智能体PPO（HAPPO）训练船载机械臂空中捕获四旋翼的协同控制策略。分布内海况0/4/5成功率最高达97.5%，与课程域随机化相当；在未见海况7/8/10上泛化更好，海况10中位成功率最高提升16%，坠毁率最多降低14%。对抗训练使策略更谨慎，超时率仅增<3%，但在严重未见海况下实现更安全回收，显示其海上自主回收潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Recovering unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in maritime environments is challenging due to wind turbulence and ship-deck motion, making it a valuable test case for alternative control and learning approaches as conventional landing approaches often become unreliable. We study simulated mid-air capture of quadrotor UAVs by a ship-mounted robotic arm, learning robust cooperative control policies with Heterogeneous-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (HAPPO) Reinforcement Learning. We train with HAPPO using a curriculum and an adversarial wind agent (HARL-AC) in NVIDIA Isaac Lab, and compare the obtained control policies against those generated through curriculum-based domain randomization and a benchmark trained on a single sea state. In-distribution evaluation on sea states $0/4/5$ shows comparable success for HARL-AC and domain randomization of up to $97.5\%$. On out-of-distribution sea states $7/8/10$, HARL-AC generalizes better, achieving up to $16\%$ higher median success rate at sea state 10, and substantially lower crash rates of up to $14\%$ compared to the domain randomization policy. Furthermore, we show that the adversarially trained policy shows more cautious behavior, slightly increasing timeouts by $<3\%$, but yields safer recovery behavior in severe, unseen conditions.
